written.text: Write a precis of the following passage and provide a suitable title:(14) Approximately 80 percent of young people who possess smartphones are capable of locating a particular video on YouTube, and of this group, 90 percent know how to share it with a friend. In addition, 70 percent can navigate the internet to seek answers to inquiries, while close to two-thirds are able to set an alarm for specific times. A little more than one-third can use Google Maps to ascertain the duration of travel between two destinations. During these digital assessments, boys tended to perform better than girls in most tasks. However, the primary factor in this case appeared to be smartphone ownership. Among those who knew how to use smartphones, 43.7 percent boys and 19.8 percent girls actually owned the smartphone. When the differences in ownership disappear, so does the difference in digital skills between boys and girls. Computer ownership was found to be far lower than smartphones (less than 10 percent), but there were similar trends in digital skill patterns. Digital literacy is directly proportional to increased access to devices. The survey clearly indicated that young people look at technology as a pathway for **creative expression**. Approximately 78 percent use their smartphones for entertainment-related activities such as watching movies or listening to music, 57 percent play games regularly, and 90 percent had used some form of social media in the previous week.

Read the passage below carefully and answer the questions that follow: India is an ancient land with a long and complex history. Throughout the centuries many races and cultures have come to this land, settled here, and contributed something to its life. Some came as conquerors, some as traders, and others as travelers in search of knowledge. Yet in spite of these many influences, India has preserved a certain unity which has held its people together. This unity does not come from uniformity. On the contrary, India is a land of remarkable diversity. There are many languages spoken in different regions, numerous religious beliefs practiced by its people, and a wide variety of customs and traditions that shape everyday life. Yet beneath this diversity there lies a deeper cultural bond. Over long periods of time, ideas, philosophies, and ways of life have interacted with one another and gradually formed a shared civilization. Pilgrimages, trade routes, literature, and philosophical discussions helped create connections between distant regions. In this way, people living in different parts of the country came to feel that they belonged to a larger cultural whole. India has often been described as a meeting place of cultures. Foreign influences were not always rejected; many were absorbed and transformed into something new. This ability to absorb and adapt has been one of the distinctive features of Indian civilization. Rather than destroying earlier traditions, new ideas were often woven into the existing fabric of society. Thus the history of India is not merely a record of kings and battles. It is also the story of how different peoples and traditions gradually learned to live together and create a shared cultural heritage. This process has given India its unique character and enduring strength. Answer the following questions;

subparts.a: How did different cultures contribute to Indian civilization?(2)
subparts.b: Where does the unity in India come from?(2)
subparts.c: What gradually formed a shared civilization?(2)
subparts.d: Why is India described as a “meeting place of cultures”?(2)
